[![CLA assistant check](https://cla-assistant.io/pull/badge/signed)](https://cla-assistant.io/casdoor/casdoor?pullRequest=6079)
All committers have signed the CLA.

Thanks for tracking this down. Copying `Cert` in `getCimdApplicationOfOrganization` is the right idea, but on its own it breaks the refresh_token grant: the token endpoint looks up the shared application by its client_id without adapting it to an organization, so `RefreshToken` verifies the refresh token with `cert-built-in` and rejects the one now signed with the organization's cert (`parse refresh token error: token signature is invalid`). Introspection, Casdoor's own MCP endpoint and token exchange have the same problem.

Fixed in https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/commit/c5610a03 instead: a shared CIMD application signs with the cert and signing method of the default application of the user's organization in every grant (authorization code, refresh, ID-JAG, logout token), and tokens are verified with the cert of the organization they were issued to. Closing this PR in favor of that commit.
